claims.text: The initial system is an elemental Cr coating on a zirconium-alloy fuel-cladding substrate.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of the unmodified Cr coating.
Approximately 5–10 at.% Al can be incorporated into the Cr coating by co-sputtering.
Adding approximately 5–10 at.% Al to Cr will induce controlled Al segregation at the Cr–Zr interface.
Oxidizing service exposure will convert the segregated Al into a continuous, uniformly distributed, nanocrystalline Al2O3 or mixed Cr2O3–Al2O3 interlayer at the buried Cr–Zr interface.
Al preferentially oxidizes to form a stable, low-diffusivity oxide barrier.
The proposed oxide barrier reduces vacancy formation and local atomic mobility at the Cr–Zr interface.
Reduced vacancy formation and atomic mobility will retard Cr–Zr interdiffusion and delay interfacial degradation.
Cr coatings possess oxidation-protective behavior that can be preserved after Al modification.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Al-doped Cr coating will exhibit a smaller Cr–Zr interdiffusion depth and delayed onset of interfacial degradation.
The Al-doped Cr coating will have improved coating integrity under prolonged simulated PWR water exposure at approximately 320 °C.
The Al-doped Cr coating will retain improved integrity and oxidation protection during steam exposure at approximately 1200 °C for hours.
Uniform Al incorporation during deposition is required to obtain the proposed continuous oxide barrier.
Deposition deviations that disrupt oxide-barrier uniformity could compromise protection.
Barrier continuity under cyclic thermal conditions and long-term service is uncertain.
Cr–Zr interdiffusion depth can be compared between elemental-Cr and Al-doped-Cr controls using cross-sectional EDS mapping and line scans after matched exposures.

The hypothesis is falsified if the Al-doped coating fails to produce a statistically significant reduction, exemplified as greater than 20%, in Cr–Zr interdiffusion depth relative to the elemental-Cr control.
The hypothesis is also deemed falsified by a discontinuous or nonuniform oxide layer or by no appreciable improvement in adhesion and mechanical integrity.
